summary: Tenant stuck on legacy model variant after rapid canary weight drift during traffic surge
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (FinNova) reports that a subset of requests have been routed to an older model variant that they had explicitly pinned away from. The regression began during a customer traffic spike and a concurrent canary weight change.

Impact:
- ~18% of requests for one tenant are receiving outputs from the legacy variant (v1.8) instead of the intended pinned variant (v2.0-quant).
- Customer reports degraded result quality and elevated token usage leading to billing concerns.
- Problem started during a scheduled weighted canary adjustment and persisted despite control-plane restarts.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated pool (dedicated tenant pool, us-east region)
- Tenant: finnova-prod (dedicated)
- Affected model: redwood/oasst-7b-v2-quant (target), legacy fallback v1.8 (observed)
- Ingress path: edge-proxy -> orchestrator -> serving-runtime (quantized GPU nodes)

Steps to reproduce (from customer and support replay):
1) Customer increases concurrent sessions from ~1200 to ~3200 over 3 minutes (traffic surge window).
2) Support triggers canary weight shift from 5% -> 25% for v2.0-quant via Console rollout UI.
3) During the shift, certain sticky sessions begin receiving v1.8 responses; session affinity indicates a pin to legacy variant.
4) Attempts to refresh tenant pin via API return success but do not clear stuck affinity for affected sessions.

Observed behaviour:
- Sessions tied to a cohort continue to route to legacy variant even after pin-update and orchestration restart.
- Edge logs show the cohort affinity token is present, but orchestrator returns placement for legacy variant for that token.
- No 5xx errors; requests succeed but with unexpected variant.

Expected behaviour:
- Pin update should immediately route all new requests and existing sessions (subject to TTL) to pinned variant or trigger a clean handoff according to rollout policy.

Logs / Dashboards / Links:
- Support trace: https://console.redwood/support/traces/SUP-142357-rt-01
- Ingress sampling (edge-proxy): https://dash.redwood/edge/proxy/requests?trace=SUP-142357
- Orchestrator placement events: https://dash.redwood/orchestrator/events?range=3h
- Customer-provided transcript showing v1.8 outputs: attached as finnova_output_snippet.txt
- Related Slack thread: #support-finnova (slack.com/archives/C02XYZ/2026-03-12)

Initial hypothesis:
- During rapid weight change + surge, pin reconciliation logic failed to pick up the new placement snapshot and served an older placement for a subset of cohort tokens.
- Edge or sidecar cache may be returning stale affinity tokens that map to older cohort epoch.
- Orchestrator snapshot merge timing could create transient window where placement resolver prefers legacy nodes for tokens with intermediate epochs.

Impact assessment so far:
- Customer-facing but limited to a cohort (approx 18% of tenant traffic).
- No increased error rates or node OOMs; primarily correctness / quality and billing exposure.

Immediate mitigation attempted:
- Force pin-refresh for finnova via admin API (admin.routing.refresh_pins(tenant=finnova-prod)) — reported success but did not clear affected live sessions.
- Rolling restart of orchestrator worker behind tenant shard performed at 2026-03-12 15:40 UTC — did not rectify stuck cohort.
- Temporary rule applied on edge to reject affinity cookies older than epoch-245 to force rebind (edge config change ID: edgecfg-2026-03-12-1346). Observed 70% of stuck sessions rebind within 6 minutes, remaining ~30% persisted.

Next steps (in progress):
- SRE to instrument placement resolver trace for token->epoch mapping (assigned).
- Routing team to review snapshot merge logic and any prefetch/caching decisions during weight changes.
- Run targeted session reshard job to clear remaining stuck cohort (requires scheduled maintenance window with customer).
- Engineering to prepare a hotfix to make pin-refresh force-evict session affinity when requested by admin API.

investigation_notes: Reproduced in staging by simulating 3-minute ramp from 1.2k -> 3.2k concurrent sessions and applying a 5%->25% canary weight shift. Traced token->placement mapping; found ~27% of tokens referenced stale epoch (one snapshot behind). Orchestrator logs show snapshot merge fences executing but a race condition in the token resolver allowed lookups against an older snapshot until its TTL expired. Edge cookie expiry workaround reduces surface but does not eliminate tokens already materialized in downstream session stores.
resolution: In progress. Short-term: targeted session rebind job executed (2026-03-13) cleared ~98% of stuck sessions. Long-term: hotfix merged to routing (PR #1987) will add admin API flag to force-evict and strict snapshot fence during canary weight changes. Hotfix rollout scheduled to dedicated control plane next build window 2026-03-15 02:00 UTC. Post-rollout validation and customer billing reconciliation scheduled. Follow-up tasks: add unit + integration tests for snapshot merge race, augment runbook with guidance for forced-rebind, and instrument more granular metrics for epoch mismatch rate.
resolution_notes: Preliminary rebind job successful; remaining items tracking in INT backlog. Customer notified and provided credit for degraded tokens. Will close once hotfix is live and post-validation is clean.
